source_views.source: Muhurta Chintamani of Rama Daivajna (with Hindi commentary; Source Library AI translation, unreviewed), ch. 6 (vivaha / marriage) v.29-30, 33 (p.97-98)
source_views.view: Gana is fixed by the birth nakshatra (Deva: Ashwini, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Pushya, Hasta, Swati, Anuradha, Shravana, Revati; Manushya: Bharani, Rohini, Ardra, Purva Phalguni, Uttara Phalguni, Purva Ashadha, Uttara Ashadha, Purva Bhadrapada, Uttara Bhadrapada; Rakshasa: Krittika, Ashlesha, Magha, Chitra, Vishakha, Jyeshtha, Mula, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha). Same gana: great affection (6 points); Deva-Manushya: middling (5); Rakshasa with Manushya: [maraka: text predicts danger to life / death]; Rakshasa with Deva: enmity (0). The commentary adds directional variants (a Manushya groom with a Rakshasa bride is the worst case). v.33: if the Moon-sign lords or navamsha lords of the couple are friends, the gana fault does not apply.

disagreements: The Jataka Bharanam verse is unusually ascetic (short stature, little food) compared with the usual reading of Deva gana as simply virtuous; the AI translator also flags this.
phrasing_guidance: Describe gana as a temperament style, not moral worth; never call anyone 'demonic'. For Rakshasa, say 'forceful, independent temperament'. In matching, mention cancellations before any warning, and never repeat a death prediction.

cancellations.condition: the lords of the couple's Moon signs, or of their navamshas, are friends

summary: Adi (first) nadi: one of three nakshatra groups used in nadi-kuta, the heaviest-weighted matching factor.
common_outcomes: used only in compatibility: both partners in the same nadi is a fault; different nadis earn the full 8 points

by_area.relationships: nadi-kuta: 8 of 36 points; same nadi is the classic 'nadi dosha'

weakeners_or_cancellations: Same nadi for both partners is a matching fault (nadi dosha).
lagna_or_context_notes: Nadi comes from the Moon's nakshatra at birth and says nothing about the person alone in the sources read; it is a matching factor.

source_views.source: Muhurta Chintamani of Rama Daivajna (with Hindi commentary; Source Library AI translation, unreviewed), ch. 6 (vivaha / marriage) v.34 (p.98-99)
source_views.view: Nadi is set by the birth nakshatra (Adi: Ashwini, Ardra, Punarvasu, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Jyeshtha, Mula, Shatabhisha, Purva Bhadrapada; Madhya: Bharani, Mrigashira, Pushya, Purva Phalguni, Chitra, Anuradha, Purva Ashadha, Dhanishta, Uttara Bhadrapada; Antya: Krittika, Rohini, Ashlesha, Magha, Swati, Vishakha, Uttara Ashadha, Shravana, Revati). Bride and groom in the same nadi is inauspicious; both in Madhya nadi: [maraka: text predicts danger to life / death]. Other views quoted: the side nadis' fault does not apply south of the Godavari or for Kshatriyas; Adi harms the groom, Antya the bride, Madhya both. If only the nakshatra (not the pada) nadi matches, the fault is minor. Remedies: Mahamrityunjaya japa and the gift of a golden nadi. Nadi purity is required even when other kuta faults are cancelled (v.32 commentary).

disagreements: Muhurta Chintamani records several views: regional exemptions for the side nadis (Adi, Antya), which partner each nadi harms, and four- and five-nadi schemes used in some regions instead of the three-nadi scheme.
phrasing_guidance: Do not describe nadi as a personal trait. In matching, state nadi dosha calmly, mention the exemptions and remedies, and never repeat a prediction of death or childlessness.

cancellations.condition: the nadi matches by nakshatra but not by pada: fault is minor
regional view: side-nadi (Adi/Antya) fault not applied south of the Godavari or for Kshatriyas

remedies.remedy: Mahamrityunjaya japa; gift of a golden nadi

summary: Yoni assigns each birth nakshatra an animal (14 animals, two nakshatras each with Abhijit); in marriage matching it measures instinctive and physical compatibility and scores 4 of 36 points.
common_outcomes: same yoni: excellent; friendly yonis: good; neutral: average; enemy yonis: inauspicious
natural enemy pairs: cow-tiger, elephant-lion, horse-buffalo, dog-deer, mongoose-serpent, monkey-sheep, cat-rat
weakeners_or_cancellations: Enemy yonis (e.g. cow-tiger) are to be avoided in a match (Muhurta Chintamani ch. 6 v.26).
lagna_or_context_notes: From the Moon's nakshatra. Animals per Muhurta Chintamani: horse (Ashwini, Shatabhisha), elephant (Bharani, Revati), sheep (Krittika, Pushya), serpent (Rohini, Mrigashira), dog (Ardra, Mula), cat (Punarvasu, Ashlesha), rat (Magha, Purva Phalguni), cow (Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Bhadrapada), buffalo (Hasta, Swati), tiger (Chitra, Vishakha), deer (Anuradha, Jyeshtha), monkey (Purva Ashadha, Shravana), mongoose (Uttara Ashadha, Abhijit), lion (Dhanishta, Purva Bhadrapada).

source_views.source: Muhurta Chintamani of Rama Daivajna (with Hindi commentary; Source Library AI translation, unreviewed), ch. 6 (vivaha / marriage) v.25-26 (p.95-96)
source_views.view: Lists the animal of each nakshatra and the seven pairs of great enmity; same or friendly yoni is good; yoni friendship earns 4 points.

disagreements: The AI-translated verse has slips (Purva Ashadha under both monkey and dog; Magha and Purva Phalguni under cat); the commentary on the next page gives the usual scheme (Ardra = dog, Magha and Purva Phalguni = rat), used here.
phrasing_guidance: Speak of yoni as one small compatibility factor; avoid sexual or animal-character language about the person.

summary: Varna ranks the Moon signs into four classes for marriage matching (1 of 36 points); it is the lowest-weighted factor and says little about the person.
common_outcomes: Brahmin: Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces; Kshatriya: Aries, Leo, Sagittarius; Vaishya: Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn; Shudra: Gemini, Libra, Aquarius
the point is given when the groom's varna is equal to or higher than the bride's
lagna_or_context_notes: From the Moon sign. It is a matching rule only; the sources read give no personal reading for it.

source_views.source: Muhurta Chintamani of Rama Daivajna (with Hindi commentary; Source Library AI translation, unreviewed), ch. 6 (vivaha / marriage) v.21-22 (p.95), table p.99
source_views.view: Lists the eight kutas with points 1-8 (varna 1, vashya 2, tara 3, yoni 4, graha maitri 5, gana 6, bhakuta 7, nadi 8; total 36): a higher score is better. Gives the sign groups for the four varnas; a bride of higher varna than the groom is not praised; same varna is best.

phrasing_guidance: Mention only inside a matching summary, as the smallest factor; do not use caste language about the person or imply social rank.

summary: Vashya groups the Moon signs (human, quadruped, water, wild, insect) to judge which partner's sign 'is controlled by' the other's; it scores 2 of 36 points in marriage matching.
common_outcomes: human signs hold all others under their control except Leo; water signs are 'food' of the human signs
all signs are under Leo except Scorpio
the points are given when the bride's sign is under the groom's sign

by_area.relationships: vashya-kuta, 2 points; read as mutual attraction or influence

lagna_or_context_notes: From the Moon sign. Human signs per the commentary: Gemini, Virgo, Libra, first half of Sagittarius, Aquarius. Muhurta Chintamani says other relations of control are to be judged 'from worldly behaviour', and its table gives half or partial points for mixed pairs.

source_views.source: Muhurta Chintamani of Rama Daivajna (with Hindi commentary; Source Library AI translation, unreviewed), ch. 6 (vivaha / marriage) v.23 (p.95), table p.99
source_views.view: Defines vashya by sign groups: human signs control all but Leo; water signs are the food of humans; all are under Leo except Scorpio; 2 points when the bride's sign is subject to the groom's. A table scores pairs of quadruped, human, water, wild and insect classes from 0 to 2.

phrasing_guidance: Explain as one small factor of attraction or influence in a match; avoid language of one partner controlling the other.
